newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Vodacom reports brisk sales.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Vodacom reports brisk sales.

text.p: South Africa's Vodacom cellular phone network said on Tuesday sales of its pre-paid "Vodago" network were exceeding expectations.

"So far more than 8,000 Vodago packages at 129.99 rand each and 8,000 recharge vouchers at 250 rand each have been sold, passing the target set for February," said a statement from Vodacom, a joint venture network operator owned by Britain's Vodafone Plc and state-run Telkom SA.

It said Vodago, introduced on November 1, had been intended to attract an additional 250,000 users to the network within two or three years but it now appeared this target could be reached by the end of next year.
"With Vodago, subscribers don't have to sign contracts, they don't have to qualify for credit and they can use any GSM cellphone. This has unlocked a whole second tier of users," Vodacom said.
